text:
Ravi Patel: Heads up — us-west2-gpu-pool-3 is seeing a spike of streaming token timeouts. Lots of gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED for chat streams, ~20s deadline hits. Started ~11:20 UTC and is still noisy. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/gpu/us-west2/pool-3

Claire Nguyen: Which nodes? any recent infra changes?

Ravi Patel: Affected nodes: gw-uw2-gpu-3[12-18]. We pushed kernel rollouts last night (daemonset: node-kernel-6-1). No config changes after that. Attaching short tcpdump around the deadline failures:  

```
13:21:03.123456 IP gw-uw2-gpu-312.443 > service-frontend.52012: Flags [.], seq 845:1290, ack 512, win 32768, length 445
13:21:03.123789 IP service-frontend.52012 > gw-uw2-gpu-312.443: Flags [.], ack 1290, win 65535, length 0
13:21:03.124010 IP gw-uw2-gpu-312.443 > service-frontend.52012: Flags [.], seq 1290:1735, ack 512, length 445
13:21:03.124210 IP service-frontend.52012 > gw-uw2-gpu-312.443: Flags [.] ack 512, win 65535, length 0 (duplicate ack)
13:21:03.124411 IP gw-uw2-gpu-312.443 > service-frontend.52012: Flags [F.], seq 1735, ack 512, length 0
```

Ravi Patel: You can see repeating small bursts and duplicate ACKs — looks like out-of-order segments or segmentation reassembly issues.

Tomas Eriksson: Could be PMTU/fragmentation or offload interactions (GRO/LRO/GSO). We saw similar after changing NIC drivers. Which NIC + MTU?

Ravi Patel: NIC: mellanox-mlx5 on those hosts. MTU is 9000. No recent MTU changes that I know of.

Serena Li: We did roll the kernel to 6.1 across the pool; the daemonset change included a firmware bump for mlx5. Might have toggled offload defaults.

Claire Nguyen: Can you run a quick iperf3 + capture for large packets and also check if PMTU discovery is failing?

Ravi Patel: Ran iperf3 between gw-uw2-gpu-312 and service-frontend:

```
# iperf3 -c service-frontend -M 16384 -l 8192 -t 30
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-30.00  sec  6.78 GBytes   1.94 Gbits/sec  (window 512 KByte)
```

Ravi Patel: iperf3 shows good throughput and ~0% loss, but application traces show latency variance and duplicate ACKs in tcpdump. netstat -s shows increased "out-of-order packets" counters.

Tomas Eriksson: Let's try disabling GRO/GSO on one node to test. Command: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off` (may also need to disable rx/tx offload depending on NIC). If this reduces reordering, it's likely offload + firmware rework.

Ravi Patel: Doing toggle now on gw-uw2-gpu-314, restarting a few affected services.

infra-bot: applied netstack-change-set/disable-gro-gso on gw-uw2-gpu-314 (rollout id: r-2026-03-18-314)

Ravi Patel: After toggle: duplicate-ack spikes dropped by ~70% in the 10m window. gRPC stream timeouts stopped for the canary node.

Claire Nguyen: Nice. Can you measure CPU delta? disabling offloads typically increases CPU on NIC-heavy flows.

Tomas Eriksson: On our test workloads cpu rose ~2.5-4% per worker, throughput stayed within 5% of baseline. Latency p99 improved by ~120ms. Worth canarying pool-wide if CPU headroom exists.

Serena Li: Scheduler: can we roll the disable-gro-gso change to gw-uw2-gpu-3[12-18] as a staged rollout? Patch template: `k8s-daemonset: net-offload-toggle` — target 25% nodes -> 50% -> 100%, monitor CPU and stream errors.

Claire Nguyen: Add alert for CPU delta > 10% and streaming error rate > baseline+1%. If both trigger, auto-rollback.

Ravi Patel: I'll start the canary now at 11:45 UTC. Will report back in 20m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-27 (type: networking, impact: streaming tokens). Linked runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/net/reordering-offloads

Tomas Eriksson: Follow-up: file bug with Mellanox firmware + kernel 6.1 combination and request firmware roll-back if vendor confirms regression.

Serena Li: Agree. Also add small test to upgrade playbook to validate GRO/GSO behavior after kernel/firmware bumps.

Ravi Patel: Update: canary shows stable streams at 12:10 UTC, CPU within expected range. Proceeding to staged rollout. Will keep channel updated. :white_check_mark:
